title: trifolium michelianum subsp. angulatum
intro: Trifolium michelianum subsp. angulatum, commonly known as the Narrow-leaved Red Clover, is a plant species belonging to the Fabaceae family, characterized by its small, pinkish-white flowers and narrow leaves. This plant has been used for its potential health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory properties, which may help to reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease, improve digestion, and alleviate symptoms of menopause. The therapeutic actions of Trifolium michelianum subsp. angulatum include its ability to act as an antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and estrogenic agent, which may contribute to its potential benefits in reducing the risk of osteoporosis and certain types of cancer. The bioactive constituents of this plant include isoflavones, particularly formononetin and genistein, which are thought to be responsible for its therapeutic actions.
